title: Lower Bounds for the Hales-Jewett Numbers via Symmetric and One-Weight Colorings
summary: The Hales-Jewett number HJ(t,r) is the least dimension n such that every r-coloring of the grid [t]^n contains a monochromatic combinatorial line. We prove HJ(3,3) >= 22 and HJ(4,2) >= 14, improving the previous records 14 and 12. The engine is an exact reduction: a coloring of [t]^n invariant under coordinate permutations descends to the discrete simplex of letter-count vectors, where a combinatorial line is precisely a corner tuple; the 4,387,586,157,901 lines of [3]^21 thereby compress to 1771 local conditions on 253 cells.
